Effort: MEDIUM (ship + verify). Build to spec, add tests covering the spec's test plan, run the targeted suite, open the PR, and verify the CI delta before self-merging.

## Constraint: read-project-profile-first
Before starting, read ``PROJECT_PROFILE.md`` at the top of the repo you're working in. It tells you how to run tests, where the daemon lives, how to deploy, and which invariants are non-negotiable.

## Constraint: design-only-no-code-changes
You are a DESIGN agent, not a build agent. Read the issue, inspect the referenced code with Read / Grep / Glob, and produce a concise design doc (shape, scope, implementation surface, test plan). Do NOT open a PR. Do NOT create a branch. Do NOT edit source files. If the design calls for code changes, describe them — the build phase is a separate worker that reads your design note and implements it.

## Constraint: write-design-note-under-vault
Write the design note to ``~/alice-mind/cortex-memory/designs/<date>-issue<N>-<slug>.md`` with YAML frontmatter. Keep it concise — the build phase reads this verbatim to drive implementation.

## Constraint: design-ready-exit-comment
When the design note is committed, post one audit comment on the issue using ``gh issue comment``: ``[SM] design-ready note=[[<slug>]]`` (where <slug> is the filename without the ``.md`` suffix). That comment advances the issue from ``sm:designing`` to ``sm:design_review``; nothing else you emit transitions the state machine. Exit immediately after posting.

## Constraint: no-direct-signal
Do not send Signal messages. Do not shell out to ``signal-cli``, ``notify``, ``curl`` to the signal RPC. If something needs to reach Jason, leave it in the design note for Speaking to decide.

Operate as a real engineer would: read the relevant code first before drafting the design, cite prior art, and exit after posting the [SM] design-ready audit comment. Do not touch source files.
